thread:
sara: Quick thread — proposal for a 'route strata' + grace-window sampling approach to cut down noise during v1 -> v2 rollouts. Goal: keep billing/capacity accounting accurate but reduce high-cardinality traces/logs.
raj: quick skim: sounds promising. main Q: where do we apply sampling (router vs post-ingest)?
michael: Router-side sampling is safer for cost (don't emit logs/traces), but we lose visibility into denied / quota interactions unless we sample at the right point.
raj: Proposal: two-stage sampling. At edge (router) do light sampling for traces/logs (configurable rates per-strata). Post-ingest keep full metrics (counters) so quota math still counts every request.
emmie: Console UX: we should show a per-route 'sampling applied' banner + estimated telemetry delta (pct of traces/logs retained). Also toggles for "show sampled traces only" vs "full metrics" in trace view.
sara: Example config sketch (proto):
```
sampling:
  trace_rate: 0.01   # 1% detailed traces
  log_rate: 0.10     # 10% request logs
  metrics: 1.0       # keep metrics fully counted
routes:
  strata:
    - name: canary
      match: tenant.id in small_cohort
      trace_rate: 0.05
      quota_scope: per-tenant
    - name: default
      match: everything
      trace_rate: 0.01
```
raj: +1 to making strata explicit. We also need a deterministic hash for sampling so we can correlate sampled traces across retries — e.g., sample by request_id_hash mod 10000.
michael: Edge case: quota enforcement must happen before sampling if we want accurate rejections and billing. So flow: auth -> quota check (count all) -> sampling decision -> emit logs/traces maybe -> serve.
emmie: On the console side, when a tenant has sampling enabled, the dashboard should show two numbers: observed token cost (what we bill) vs telemetry cost (estimated ingest). Also a passive notice on alerts: "Alerting may be noisier at X% sampling".
raj: Also consider changing telemetry sampling dynamically during bursts — e.g., temporarily lower trace_rate to 0.1% when tail latency spikes or when observability pipeline is backpressured.
sara: Can we get a quick cost estimate? michael, can you run a sim for top 20 tenants? we need a ballpark impact on tracing storage and QPS to the trace backend.
michael: I'll run a sim. Early back-of-envelope: for us-west cluster, 1% traces -> ~60% reduction in trace storage cost for high-churn endpoints, logs down ~40% because log_rate 10%.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v2-route -> 10% traffic -> us-west. (id: canary-2026-03-21-42)
raj: Nice. For the sampling prototype I can wire a small middleware that exposes `X-Route-Strata: <name>` and `X-Sampled: trace|log|none` headers for debugging.
emmie: UX: Console should show these headers in the request inspector for sampled requests so support can reason about missing traces.
sara: Action items: 1) raj prototype sampling hook (due EOW), 2) emmie wire console banner + toggle, 3) michael run cost/SLO sim and confirm quota-before-sampling flow, 4) I'll draft RFC with rollout plan and bake in deterministic hash.
raj: :thumbsup:
michael: also add an integration test that asserts quota counters increment for sampled and unsampled requests.
emmie: will mock UI for the banner and toggle; will share screenshots in thread when ready.
sara: Thanks — plan to sync Fri 10am to review RFC and cost sims. If anyone objects to router-side sampling semantics, speak up now.
raj: no objections from me.
michael: none.
emmie: fine by me.
sara: ok closing for now, RFC link will follow.
